free_tier.stated: Anyone can create a free account and run Jupyter notebooks on SciServer Compute containers that sit next to the hosted data. The persistent quota is 10 GB per user and "you may only create up to three containers". The site describes its purpose as letting researchers work with terabytes or petabytes "without needing to download any large datasets", and the default image ships Python 3.7, R 3.6.2, Jupyter Notebook 6.0.3, JupyterLab 1.2.6, TensorFlow 2.0.0 and PyTorch 1.4.0.

chaining: The composition is data locality rather than raw capacity: SciServer hosts SDSS, GALEX and Gaia releases next to the containers, so a 10 GB quota is not a limit on the analysis because the terabyte inputs never enter the user volume, which is the opposite trade from every other free tier in documented records.

limits.value: 10 GB of persistent storage per user is the hard ceiling, temporary volumes carry no quota but are deleted after a stated grace period, and no CPU or memory quota per container is published anywhere read.
